skills.name: candidates
skills.description: Bounded table of public catalog products that pass explicit filters (category, form, wavelength, readiness, numeric ranges with units), sorted by closeness to a value or by a field. Use it to pick catalog parts for a requirement.

skills.name: compare
skills.description: Compare saved runs, or the samples of a sweep study, by target and observation-plane ID without rerunning; lists differing inputs, deltas to a reference run and, with a current Project, each run's freshness. Use it to explain what an edit changed.

skills.name: contrib-case
skills.description: Turn a finished os-optics design into a PR-ready os-optics-kit case: engine-verified project.json, CASE.md, README with rendered images, expected outcome and a git patch. Use when the user wants to share a design as a case.

skills.name: contrib-tool
skills.description: Package a helper script as an os-optics-kit command with its skill page and tests, verified and exported as a PR-ready git patch. Use when a helper is useful beyond one design or case.

skills.name: edit
skills.description: List a Project's objects with editable values, units and frames, then apply edit operations by object ID with explicit units, checked by the engine and written atomically to a new file (optionally run). Use it to change a design reproducibly.

skills.name: measurements
skills.description: Subtract backgrounds from detector CSV data, optionally normalize by a reference channel, and fit a straight line with residuals, a plot and a provenance record; the input file is never modified. Use it to analyze a measured response curve.

skills.name: plot
skills.description: Draw standard PNG and SVG plots from saved results without simulating - sweep curves or two-parameter heatmaps with target bounds, the power distribution of a run, signed bar charts and histograms. Use it to show study or run results.

skills.name: present
skills.description: Prepare slide-ready material from saved runs and studies - system views, result plots, comparisons, animations, an offline gallery and a portable bundle - and restyle it (language, background, text and figure size) from a saved configuration without simulating.
skills.requires: os-optics>=0.13,<0.14; os-optics-kit[plot]; os-optics-kit[render] for views and animations; os-optics-kit[media] for MP4

skills.name: render
skills.description: Render reproducible 3D figures with camera angles, roll, element framing and a manifest.

skills.name: report
skills.description: Assemble a factual Markdown and JSON report from a sweep study or saved runs without rerunning - identity, inputs, edits, target outcomes, counts with denominators, diagnostics, freshness, plots and an artifact list with sha256. Use it to hand results to a person.

skills.name: run-case
skills.description: Find an engine-reproducible OS Optics case, copy it, run it, check it against its recorded outcome and adapt it. Use when a worked design close to the user's question exists or a known-good starting Project is needed.

skills.name: sensitivity
skills.description: Finite-difference sensitivity of selected targets to explicit design parameters, with two step sizes checked against each other and every sample saved; ranks parameters per target. Use it to find which positions, angles or values a target depends on most.

skills.name: summary
skills.description: Read a saved os-optics run directory into one compact JSON document (targets, assessments, power budget, issues, identity) with an exit code per requirement outcome. Use it after every run before deciding anything.

skills.name: sweep
skills.description: Run a bounded one- or two-parameter sweep of a Project from a JSON spec; every sample's Project and run are saved, counted by outcome, and ranked by an optional objective under constraints. Use it to explore a design parameter.

skills.name: tolerance
skills.description: Seeded tolerance study - draw independent offsets from declared uniform or truncated-normal distributions, save the sample set before any run, run and count every sample, and report target distributions. Use it to estimate how often a design meets its targets.
